tips.title: Subjects keep their article
tips.body: *J'aime **les** maths, je déteste l'histoire, je suis fort en **français**.* After an opinion verb the subject keeps *le / la / les / l'* — the same rule as the opinions topic. It drops after **en** (*fort en maths, nul en dessin*) and in timetable talk (*on a maths le lundi*).

tips.title: Maths and sciences are plural
tips.body: *Les maths **sont** difficiles. Les sciences **sont** intéressantes.* Both are plural feminine in French, so the verb and the adjective are plural too. *Le math* does not exist.

tips.title: Fort en, nul en, doué pour
tips.body: *Je suis **fort(e) en** maths* (good at), *je suis **nul(le) en** dessin* (rubbish at), *je suis **doué(e) pour** la musique* (gifted at). *En* takes no article, *pour* keeps one. These three phrases answer any "which subjects are you good at" question.

tips.title: Le prof est, le cours est
tips.body: Say why, not just what: *j'aime la géo **parce que le prof est sympa** / **parce que les cours sont intéressants***. The reason is usually about the teacher or the lessons, and it is where the marks are.

tips.title: Une matière, not un sujet
tips.body: **Une matière** is a school subject. *Un sujet* is a topic or an essay question — a false friend. *Ma matière préférée, c'est …* is the phrase to have ready.

why.matters: School is the topic you can always talk about, which is why the exam keeps asking about it: your subjects, your reasons, your timetable and your day. The French runs on articles and agreement. *Une matière* keeps its article after an opinion verb and loses it after *en*; *les maths* and *les sciences* are plural and take plural verbs; and every adjective agrees with the subject, not with you. Reasons are the part that earns, and the topic gives five kinds so that an opinion about geography never has to be *c'est intéressant* twice.

examples.title: The timetable on the fridge
examples.body: *L'emploi du temps* is a grid of subjects with their articles built in, and the article is what you need first: *le français, la géographie, l'histoire, les maths*. The gender sets the adjective later, so *la chimie est difficile* and *les maths sont utiles* are two different agreements on the same fridge. Say each subject with its article as a single word and the grammar takes care of itself when the opinion arrives.

visual.alt: A table of school subjects with their articles and an adjective agreeing with each, including the plural les maths sont difficiles

examples.title: Fort en maths: the article that drops
examples.body: After an opinion verb the article stays, *j'adore les maths*; after *en* it goes, *je suis fort en maths*, *je suis nulle en dessin*. Getting both right in one sentence, *j'adore les maths parce que je suis forte en maths*, shows a rule rather than a habit, and *doué pour la musique* keeps its article to prove you know the difference.

examples.title: Le lundi, every Monday
examples.body: *Le lundi j'ai deux heures de maths* means every Monday; *lundi j'ai un contrôle* means this coming Monday. The article turns a day into a habit, and a listening question about someone's week hangs on it. The same day-by-day description gives you *par semaine*, the places in the school, and the complaint every French pupil makes: *il y a trop de devoirs* and *on n'a pas assez de temps*.

steps.title: Les matières
steps.body: A school subject is **une matière**, not *un sujet*. Every subject carries its article, and you need the gender because adjectives and pronouns depend on it: *le français, la géographie, l'histoire, les maths*. **Masculine**: *le français, le dessin, l'anglais, l'espagnol, l'allemand* (German). **Feminine**: *la géographie* (*la géo*), *la physique, la chimie, la biologie, la musique, l'histoire, l'informatique* (IT), *l'EPS* (PE — *l'éducation physique et sportive*), *la technologie*. **Plural**: *les maths, les sciences* — and they take **plural** verbs and adjectives: *les maths **sont** difficiles*. **Saying what you study**: *j'étudie le français, j'apprends l'espagnol* (I am learning), *je fais de la musique*, *j'ai dix matières*, *on a maths le lundi*. **Opinions keep the article**: *j'adore **les** maths, je déteste **la** chimie, je préfère l'histoire*. **But en drops it**: *je suis fort en maths, je suis nul en dessin*.

steps.title: Pourquoi ? Les raisons
steps.body:
An opinion about a subject is worth little without a **reason**, and the reasons here are a fixed set.

**About the subject**: *c'est intéressant, utile* (useful), *facile* (easy), *difficile, ennuyeux, passionnant, compliqué, pratique*.

**About the teacher**: *le prof est sympa / patient / marrant / trop sévère* (too strict) / *ennuyeux*; *le prof explique bien* (explains well); *on s'entend bien avec le prof*.

**About the lessons**: *les cours sont intéressants*, *on fait des expériences* (experiments), *on travaille en groupe*, *il y a trop de devoirs* (too much homework), *on doit apprendre par cœur* (learn by heart).

**About yourself**: *je suis fort(e) en …*, *je comprends tout* (I understand everything), *j'ai de bonnes notes*, *je trouve ça facile* (I find it easy).

**Careful with the agreement**: the adjective agrees with the **subject**, which has a gender. *La chimie est difficile, le français est intéressant, les maths sont utiles, l'histoire est passionnante.*

**Intensity**: *assez, très, un peu, trop, vraiment* (really). *Je trouve la physique **vraiment** difficile.*

steps.title: L'emploi du temps et la journée
steps.body:
**The timetable** is *l'emploi du temps*, and talking about it needs days, times and frequency.

**Days**: *le lundi* = on Mondays (with the article); *lundi* alone = this Monday. *On a EPS **le** mardi et **le** vendredi.*

**How much**: *on a **quatre heures** de maths **par semaine***. 4 hours a week over 6 weeks is 24 hours — the kind of sum a reading text sets.

**When**: *le premier cours commence à huit heures*, *on a une heure d'étude* (study period), *la récréation est à dix heures*, *je mange à la cantine à midi*.

**Facilities**: *une salle de classe* (classroom), *un laboratoire, la bibliothèque / le CDI* (the school library), *un terrain de sport, une salle d'informatique, la cour* (playground).

**Getting there**: *je vais au collège **à pied / en bus / en voiture / à vélo***. *Le trajet dure vingt minutes* (the journey takes).

**Options**: *j'ai choisi l'espagnol comme troisième langue* (as a third language), *je fais du latin en option*, *l'année prochaine je vais faire …*

steps.title: Your turn
steps.body:
**Part A.**

1. Write six subjects with their correct articles.
2. Which two subjects are plural in French?
3. Translate: *my favourite subject is biology.*

**Part B.**

4. Give an opinion of three subjects, each with a different kind of reason.
5. Write what you are good at and bad at, using *fort en* and *nul en*.
6. Say how many hours of French you have a week and on which days.

**Part C.**

7. Write a sentence with *trop de* about homework.
8. Say which option you chose and why.
9. Write six sentences about your subjects: a favourite with two reasons, one you dislike with a reason, what you are good at, and your timetable.

For question 9, check the article on every subject and the agreement of every adjective.

steps.title: Going deeper
steps.body:
**Keep the article — except after en and in timetable talk.** *J'adore **les** maths* but *je suis fort **en** maths*. Getting both right in one sentence shows you know the rule rather than a habit.

**Agree with the subject, not with yourself.** *La chimie est difficile*, *les maths sont utiles*, *l'histoire est passionnante*. The gender of the school subject drives the adjective.

**Vary the reason.** A list of *c'est intéressant* five times is one idea repeated. Mix the subject, the teacher, the lessons, yourself and the workload.

**Use trop de and assez de.** *Il y a trop de devoirs, on n'a pas assez de temps.* Quantity + *de* with no article.

**Distinguish lundi from le lundi.** One is a date, the other a habit, and a timetable answer needs the habitual one.

**Bring in a past and a future.** *L'année dernière j'ai fait de l'allemand, mais cette année j'ai choisi l'espagnol, et l'année prochaine je vais continuer.* Three tenses inside a school answer.

**Use trouver + ça.** *Je trouve ça passionnant, je trouve la physique difficile.* *Trouver* is a more sophisticated opinion verb than *aimer*, and it takes a direct object plus an adjective.

**Avoid the false friends.** *Une matière* (not *un sujet*), *le collège* (not *college*), *passer un examen* = to **sit** an exam, not to pass it — that is *réussir*.

steps.title: Summary
steps.body:
- **Une matière** = a school subject (*un sujet* is a false friend).
- Subjects keep their article after opinion verbs: *j'adore **les** maths*.
- The article **drops after en**: *fort en maths, nul en dessin*.
- *Doué **pour** la musique* keeps the article.
- **Les maths** and **les sciences** are plural: *sont difficiles*.
- Adjectives agree with the **subject**: *l'histoire est passionnante*.
- Reasons: the subject, the teacher, the lessons, yourself, the workload.
- *Il y a **trop de** devoirs; on n'a pas **assez de** temps.*
- *Le lundi* = on Mondays; *lundi* = this Monday.
- *On a quatre heures de maths **par semaine**.*
- Places: *le CDI, un laboratoire, la cour, la cantine*.
- *J'ai choisi l'espagnol **en option**.*
- **Passer** un examen = to sit it; **réussir** = to pass it.
- *Je trouve ça …* for a stronger opinion.

examTechnique.body:
Keep the article on a subject after an opinion verb and drop it after **en**; remember *les maths* and *les sciences* are **plural**, and agree every adjective with the subject's own gender.

Give a **different kind of reason** each time — the subject, the teacher, the lessons, yourself, the workload — and add timetable detail with *le lundi* and *par semaine*. *Passer* an exam is to sit it; *réussir* is to pass it.
examinerErrors: Adjectives agreeing with the speaker rather than the subject.
Using mardi where le mardi is meant.
Repeating c'est intéressant as the only reason.
Passer un examen to mean passing it.
examTechnique.grade9Looks: A grade 9 answer keeps every article where it belongs and drops it after *en* and in timetable talk (*on a maths le lundi*), treats *les maths* and *les sciences* as plural, and agrees each adjective with the subject rather than the writer. It gives several kinds of reason, quantifies with *trop de* and *pas assez de*, uses *le lundi* for habits and *par semaine* for load, moves between last year's and next year's options, and never confuses *passer* with *réussir*.
